subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which method involves periods of work followed by periods of rest or recovery?
questions.explain: Interval training alternates bouts of work with rest periods.

questions.q: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body is known as:
questions.explain: Abduction is movement of a body part away from the midline, such as raising the arm sideways.

questions.q: The ruler drop test is used to measure:
questions.explain: The ruler drop test measures reaction time by recording how far a ruler falls before it is caught.

questions.q: Avoiding boredom by varying training is the principle of training known as:
questions.explain: The tedium principle means varying training to keep it interesting and maintain motivation.

questions.q: Movement of a limb forwards and backwards, such as kicking, occurs in which plane?
questions.explain: The sagittal plane divides the body into left and right and allows flexion and extension movements.

questions.q: Specificity as a principle of training means:
options: Training should be varied to avoid boredom
Training must match the demands of the activity
Fitness is lost when you stop
questions.explain: Specificity means training should be relevant to the sport and the components of fitness it requires.

questions.q: Which of the following is a long-term effect of regular aerobic training on the heart?
questions.explain: Cardiac hypertrophy increases stroke volume, so the heart pumps more per beat and resting heart rate falls.

questions.q: What do the letters FITT stand for?
questions.explain: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type - principles used to apply overload.

questions.q: Which joint type is found at the elbow and knee?
questions.explain: The elbow and knee are hinge joints allowing flexion and extension only.

questions.q: Which energy system provides energy for an explosive movement lasting up to about 10 seconds, such as a sprint start?
questions.explain: The ATP-PC system provides immediate energy without oxygen for short, maximal efforts of up to around 10 seconds.

questions.q: A biceps curl uses which class of lever, with the effort between the fulcrum and the load?
questions.explain: A biceps curl is a third-class lever: the effort (muscle) lies between the fulcrum (elbow) and the load (hand).

questions.q: Circuit training is best described as:
options: Lifting one heavy weight to failure
A series of exercise stations completed in turn
Running at a constant steady pace for a long time
questions.explain: Circuit training involves moving between a series of stations, each with a different exercise.

questions.q: The vertical jump test (Sargent jump) is used to measure which component of fitness?
questions.explain: The vertical jump test measures explosive leg power.

questions.q: Continuous training is most suitable for developing which component of fitness?
questions.explain: Continuous training at a steady pace for a sustained period develops aerobic, cardiovascular endurance.

questions.q: Where does gas exchange take place in the lungs?
questions.explain: Gas exchange occurs across the thin walls of the alveoli, where oxygen diffuses into the blood.

questions.q: Gradually making training harder over time so the body keeps adapting is called:
questions.explain: Progressive overload means gradually increasing the demands of training to keep improving.

questions.q: Which component of fitness is the ability to move the whole body quickly and change direction?
questions.explain: Agility is the ability to change direction quickly while keeping control of the body.

questions.q: Standing on tiptoes (plantar flexion at the ankle) is an example of which class of lever?
questions.explain: Rising onto the toes is a second-class lever: the load is between the fulcrum (toes) and the effort (calf).

questions.q: Power is best defined as:
options: The ability to keep going without tiring
The maximum force a muscle can exert
The range of movement at a joint
questions.explain: Power combines strength and speed, e.g. an explosive jump or sprint start.

questions.q: The Illinois agility run test measures a performer's:
questions.explain: The Illinois agility run test assesses how quickly a performer can change direction.

questions.q: Fartlek training is best described as:
options: Training at a constant steady pace
Short maximal sprints with full rest
questions.explain: Fartlek, meaning 'speed play', varies intensity and terrain, developing both aerobic and anaerobic fitness.

questions.q: Aerobic exercise is best described as exercise performed:
questions.explain: Aerobic means 'with oxygen' - energy is produced using oxygen during lower-intensity, longer-duration exercise.
